blocks.text: Have you ever wondered what the queer community in East London looked like in the years 2005-2015?
You’ll find the answers in The East London Years , this vibrant limited-edition new photo book by Ralf Obergfell .
“I wanted to create a homage to the East London of the Noughties and its protagonists who helped shape a cultural movement that laid the foundations for future generations.” – Ralf Obergfell –

It’s a vital document and celebration of a lost subculture captured in real time – a reminder of an era of living in the moment instead of chasing likes online – and, at a time when LGBTQIA+ rights are under threat, a testament to the defiant power of radical queer community.

As co-creator of legendary party GutterSlut, Ralf Obergfell was in the thick of it. He takes us deep inside iconic parties and venues like Trailer Trash, Gay Bingo and the first Horse Meat Disco at NYC Downlow at Glastonbury Festival. We also go to Wolfgang Tillmans’s legendary studio party at Between Bridges. And to the Dalston back alley that was home to Obergfell’s queer family, his studio experiments, iconic supper club The Pale Blue Door and three lovely chickens.

The East London Years features contributions from alt-drag pioneer Jonny Woo, Pale Blue Door creator and set designer Tony Hornecker, cultural critic Ben Walters and East London icons Gilbert & George, plus more than 50 first-hand accounts and memories from the people Obergfell photographed.
It’s about a time before gentrification, social media and political turmoil went into overdrive – a world of art, love, DIY community spirit and pleasure – a homage to Noughties Glamour and Trash.

Ralf Obergfell : The East London Years : A Homage to Glamour and Trash Foreword: Jonny Woo Texts: Ben Walters, Tony Hornecker, Ralf Obergfell Art Direction & Design: Benjamin Wolbergs Hardcover: Circular die-cut on front cover and title embossing 240 pp. (4/4 colour) 240 illustrations (176 photographs – analogue and digital) 21.5 × 29 cm (8.4 × 11.4 in)
